source.title: On the effectiveness of limited-data large language model fine-tuning for Arabic

record.file_problem: None; the full paper is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests downstream-performance predictability using fine-tuning data-size curves and a different measure (macro-F1), rather than testing pretraining loss scaling.
record.gate_note: The study reports a fine-tuning data-size sweep on ArSAS and uses the GPT-4o mini curve to predict GPT-4o scores. It does not measure held-out pretraining cross-entropy, parameter/token/compute scaling during pretraining, or compute-optimal allocation. Results on the other datasets, and the study's cited results from other work, do not test those claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study fits a logarithmic curve of downstream macro-F1 against fine-tuning tokens for GPT-4o mini on ArSAS. It then checks whether that curve predicts GPT-4o's fine-tuned scores. This is a new setting for V6: the scale axis is supervised fine-tuning data, not pretraining scale or pretraining loss. The measure is task F1, not held-out loss, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested. T3 fits better than T2 because the scaled quantity differs from the original question.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that ArSAS fine-tuning macro-F1 rises with fine-tuning data, roughly logarithmically in trained tokens, with the largest gains at small sizes. They report that GPT-4o mini's growth function, anchored at GPT-4o's 50-sample score, predicts GPT-4o's scores within 0.005. They also conclude that GPT-4o beats GPT-4o mini by under 1% and needs fewer labelled examples, and that small models can therefore estimate larger models' fine-tuning outcomes.
record.recipe_differences: The original studies concern pretraining held-out loss across model, token, or compute scales. This paper measures downstream macro-F1 after supervised fine-tuning and fits a logarithmic function of fine-tuning tokens. It is not a replication of the original method.
record.method_sensitivity: Fine-tuning batch size differs across GPT-4o mini data-size settings; the paper notes this as a potential issue. GPT-4o mini and GPT-4o use the same stated automated hyperparameter-selection approach.
record.problems: The scaling curve is fit to only five nonzero ArSAS data-size points for GPT-4o mini, and the cross-model prediction is tested on four points for GPT-4o. The paper does not report uncertainty estimates for those scaling-curve points or prediction errors. It omits GPT-4o fine-tuning on the full dataset, and its authors note that batch sizes differ across GPT-4o mini settings.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying results left out. The limited-data results for ASND and ArSarcasm, repeated-run estimates, and other cited baselines are not rows for V6's scaling-curve prediction test.

untested.parts: Prediction of downstream performance from pretraining loss or pretraining compute. Scaling across many model sizes with stated parameter counts. Tasks other than ArSAS sentiment, and fine-tuning scales above about 1.35M tokens.

missing.what: GPT-4o vs GPT-4o mini macro-F1 on ArSAS at 100 samples (0.783 vs 0.778) and 500 samples (0.790 vs 0.781), from the same splits and hyperparameters. This is a model-scale comparison bearing on V6.
Fitted curve parameters (a ≈ 0.01604, b ≈ 0.00231 for Eq 11; a ≈ 0.01604, intercept ≈ 0.588 for Eq 8). No goodness-of-fit or uncertainty is reported for the fit.

record.verdict_notes: The cross-model 'prediction' uses GPT-4o's own first point as the anchor, so only the slope transfers from GPT-4o mini; r12 is not an independent test. Batch size and epochs differ across data-size settings (1 epoch for 8,425 and 16,851 samples, 3 otherwise). This confounds the data-size curve, though the token-count axis partly addresses it. There is no full-dataset run for GPT-4o. Macro-F1 is bounded, so the log form cannot extrapolate far. The study does not bear on the original pretraining-loss claims (V1–V5, V7).

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of held-out pretraining loss for runs orders of magnitude larger.
The compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and its trend with compute.
Effects of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Whether the same held-out-loss power law applies to other modalities or regimes. The paper studies supervised fine-tuning performance, but measures macro-F1 rather than held-out loss.
Tests downstream macro-F1 prediction only for ArSAS fine-tuning, using GPT-4o mini and GPT-4o. It does not test prediction from pretraining loss or across a broad range of models, tasks, or scales.
Does not vary fitting choices to assess their effect on the original scaling exponents or compute-optimal split.

relationships.condition: GPT-4o mini, ArSAS, fine-tuning tokens from 11.6k to 1.35M
relationships.reason: Macro-F1 rises monotonically, 0.736 to 0.812, close to linear in log(tokens); the log fit tracks all five points (r2–r6). Rests on five points with no goodness-of-fit statistic.
relationships.display_finding: Macro-F1 rose from 0.736 to 0.812, approximately linearly in log tokens, across five points without a reported goodness-of-fit statistic.

relationships.condition: GPT-4o fine-tuned scores at 500, 1,000 and 8,425 samples, predicted from the curve fitted to GPT-4o mini
relationships.reason: Predicted and actual macro-F1 differ by at most 0.005 at the three non-anchor points (r13–r15). Model sizes are unstated and the two models score within about 1% of each other.
relationships.display_finding: Predicted and measured macro-F1 differed by at most 0.005 at three non-anchor points, while the two models scored within about 1% of each other.

relationships.condition: No fine-tuning (zero-shot), GPT-4o vs GPT-4o mini
relationships.reason: The presumably larger GPT-4o scores lower zero-shot (0.680 vs 0.703; r7, r1). Model scale alone does not predict the downstream ordering without adaptation. Parameter counts are not stated.
relationships.display_finding: GPT-4o scored 0.680 versus GPT-4o mini's 0.703, although their parameter sizes were unspecified.
